lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: Check that the phone number and portfolio link are real, current, and appropriate to share.
Make relevant embedded projects easy to find through the code link.
Clarify whether the test time is an average or another measure.
items.because: The before-and-after time is easier to interpret with its measurement basis.

items.says: Mention the implementation or test platform if useful.
items.because: It could establish the technical scope.

items.says: Clarify the product or time period behind the return percentages.
items.because: The result needs a clearer basis.

items.says: Clarify whether the solder-paste change was confirmed as the cause.
items.because: Identifying a likely cause is different from validating it.

items.says: Clarify whether you authored, validated, or rolled out the calibration procedure.
items.because: Your contribution is not fully clear.

items.says: Make clear that the figures are complaint counts per quarter.
items.because: They are not direct measurements of calibration drift.

items.says: Clarify whether the throughput rates were measured at the same station under comparable conditions.
items.because: That makes the before-and-after rates easier to interpret.

items.says: Say whether the fixture was built and deployed, if relevant.
items.because: The bullet says only that it was designed.

items.says: Specify what “update speed” means and how the 60% change was measured.
items.because: “Update speed” is ambiguous.

items.says: Include the deployment scope if known.
Add the test area or what the hardware-in-the-loop rig verified.
items.because: It would better convey the work.

items.says: Clarify how the logger contributed to finding the failures’ causes.
items.because: The wording implies it alone identified every root cause.

items.says: Sampling a 5 kHz signal at 8 kHz cannot capture it without aliasing as claimed.
items.because: A 5 kHz signal needs a sampling rate greater than 10 kHz, with practical acquisition also depending on filtering.

items.says: Declaring the shared counter `volatile` does not by itself fix the race condition.
items.because: It does not make access atomic or safe between an interrupt handler and the main loop.

items.says: Clarify the time period and basis for the jitter and field-fault comparisons.
items.because: The outcome metrics need to be easier to interpret.

items.says: The motor-controller work and results overlap with the Formula Student claims.
items.because: The same work and results should not appear as separate accomplishments unless they happened in both contexts.

items.says: Replace the promotional wording with concrete project scope or technical detail.
items.because: It does not tell the reader what you built or did, and its innovation and sustainability claims are unsupported.

items.says: Clarify how average current was measured and under what operating conditions.
items.because: That would make the reduction easier to interpret.

items.says: Robot-fleet motor-controller work does not fit the Formula Student project as presented.
items.because: It resembles the Voltline work, so its employer, project, and dates need verification.

items.says: Clarify your contribution to the dashboard CAN-bus firmware.
items.because: The passive construction obscures your specific role.

items.says: Explain what testing against the motor controller established.
The roughly 300-robot fleet and motor-control results duplicate the Voltline accomplishment.
items.because: Without verification that this was a separate project, it is a significant credibility risk.

items.says: If this was separate work, distinguish the project and clarify your contribution.
items.because: The distinction is not clear as written.

items.says: Organize the tools entries by type.
items.because: The category mixes languages, a platform, and an instrument.

items.says: Add relevant evidence for C++ elsewhere if it matters to your target roles.
items.because: C++ appears in Skills but is not supported elsewhere in the résumé.

items.says: Reorganize the methods entries by type.
items.because: Firmware and CAN are not methods in the same sense as hardware-in-the-loop testing or low-power design.
